Since the beginning of time, evil has always ravaged these lands. Cookies scattered through the wind as flavorless powder. Kingdoms fell at nothing but a whim. Brothers turned on brothers with nothing but a lie. Many rotted under the sweetest poison. And some…some were taken captive, to be silenced forever. And yet…every time the Beasts cause their ruin, something else sparks in the heart of cookies. Because for every darkness that rises, there are always those who oppose it. Because these Beasts don’t fight for Kingdoms, nor for peace. They fight for dominion. To them, ruin is creation. So the story begins. The call has been heard across kingdoms and the Ancients were never the only heroes around.

Looking at the place where he once taught students, now rampant with what remained of the staff, consumed by dark moon magic, it could almost make him laugh. “Carry the light you have been given,” they spoke, “and shape this world into something worthy.”

They both love to lie in the sun with their wings stretched out, though the places where they choose to lie are increasingly funnier by the day. He instead lets them roam the island, as the gales always tattle where they are anyway.

“PURE VANILLA! WHAT ARE YOU DOING?!” Hollyberry roared, hammering her fists against the shimmering forcefield. Without her Soul Jam or shield, she could do nothing but watch.
Pure Vanilla’s voice was calm, resolute. “Forgive me.”
He lifted his staff. Dark light gathered at its tip. Impossible, forbidden.
Gasps broke across the battlefield. Even Dark Enchantress faltered, shock flashing in her crimson eyes. Their magics collided, a cataclysm of light and shadow. The explosion ripped the Soul Jams from her grip, scattering them across Earthbread.
When the dust cleared, Pure Vanilla was gone.
He fell into the void. Endless, soundless. No air, no ground, only the hollow rush of falling.
Then a voice, vast and gentle, filled the emptiness:
“You are not ready to return. I will send you where you may rest, until the time comes.”
He closed his eyes. Feeling the cold embrace of the void.
 
Until a voice interrupted the Light of Truth itself.

Fount hummed thoughtfully, her gaze flicking up to the setting sun. She couldn't lie—her mind had wandered quite a bit during the picnic, her thoughts drifting to a tangle of half-formed worries and thoughts. But now, as they walked, she felt a calm settle over her. "Perhaps I was a bit… distracted." She said finally, voice soft. "The Spring Equinox is soon, and I've been worried about the preparations for quite a long time now." Salt's grip on her hand tightened ever so slightly, his voice steady as a heartbeat. "The tides don't rush the moon, my lady." A pause. "And the Equinox won't arrive a moment before it’s meant to." He turned his head just enough to catch her eyes in profile—the sunset painting them molten gold: "You’ve poured enough of your light into these preparations already… Let me carry some of that weight for you tonight?"
Fount huffed out a laugh, her lips curling into an amused smile. The thought of letting someone take on her stresses was both tantalizing and worrying in equal parts. But she was growing more and more tired. "I would rather do this on my own." She answered finally, though her smile took on a hint of teasing.

One day you're playing your favorite game only for your two favorite characters to suddenly come to life...
Now Juniper's normal day to day life has become an absolute roller coaster...
_____
 
My gaze snaps away from the yellow creature and towards the sound.Only to see the blue creature standing up. I notice how it’s about the size of a sippy cup. Like- slightly shorter than those long sippy cups.
“Where am I?” It hisses. I blink at it. It’s positioned in such a way that it seems like it is trying to be intimidating. Wide stance and all. “Answer me, you witch!”
I open my mouth and then close it. Then open it again. “Umm… my room?”
It glares at me. Eyes narrowing as its hair rises the same way a cat's hackles would rise if threatened. “Your room?” it scoffed. “Pathetic! I’ve seen sugar mines that have more dignity than this place.”
I gawk at him. “Okay, first of all, rude. Second, I hate the fact you can talk back.”

Including her treasure who had helped her against her own wishes, who dragged her out of the pit of self loathing and desolation, who restored her faith in herself.
Her advisor, her general, her smoke. All hers.

She decides to survey the kingdom to settle her nerves, to take her mind away from any imminent danger. Yet, her mind seemed unable to stop reminding her of and reliving memories of one of her most precious treasures.
What were they? After everything, was he still hers?

summary:
After everything that happened, Hazelnut Cookie left.
She didn’t announce it for sympathy from the others.
 She told Pure Vanilla Cookie at least.
He seemed.. upset, maybe that was his endless compassion.
She didn’t press further.
One morning she simply packed what she owned, a carriage already waiting for her, traveling until the wind grew sharp and cold and carried the scent of iron and pine.
She chose the Dark Cacao Kingdom for a reason.
No one there looked at her like she might shatter.
The kingdom was harsh, but it was honest. The air bit at her frosting, the soldiers spoke plainly, and no one softened their voices around her as though she were made of spun sugar.
She had been working there for about a week.
For the first time in months, she found herself smiling without forcing it.
That afternoon, Hazelnut Cookie sat alone in the courtyard with a cup of mushroom coffee warming her hand. Frost dusted the stone beneath her feet, and the sky above hung low and gray, heavy with quiet.
Footsteps approached.
Another cookie sat beside her without asking.
Not too close.Just close enough.

Sage doesn’t remember falling, but they do remember the impact.
Waking up in a reality not your own is a startling realization. It breaks you in a way you never thought possible. Suddenly everything is new and no one knows you, not the real you, and no one ever will… Nothing makes sense, but Sage always takes the truth for cold, hard facts.
It's a fact that they are now in a fantasy novel. It’s a fact that they are now a cookie. It’s a fact that “Sage” has possessed the body of “Shadow Milk”. It’s a fact that they must survive this cold, harsh reality they have now found themself in.
They are being watched. They are being hunted. They are losing this battle of mental fortitude, and Sage isn’t sure they can make it out alive.

The Fount of Knowledge has existed since the beginning of time. He is Knowledge itself, Knowledge personified. Knowledge doesn't try to do much outside of his duties. It makes things easier for everybody.

Knowledge thinks that by guiding this cookie in the right direction, it would help the issue with his Souljam that hasn’t been responding to him for reasons Knowledge can’t understand.
Truthless Recluse thinks that by accepting Knowledge’s offer of mentorship, he’ll be able to shift Knowledge’s way of thinking. He assumes Knowledge doesn’t know the truth- or at least ignores it for a reason the Recluse doesn’t quite understand. Truthless Recluse wants Knowledge to be better (and admit that he is right), and to do that Truthless needs Knowledge to see the error in his ways.

summary:
Villanelle: A highly structured 19 line poem with French origins, consisting of five tercets and one quatrain. It features a strict rhyme scheme and two repeating refrains.
 
Truthless Recluse had noticed a change between himself and the Sage. It was only small, almost imperceptible, but undeniable. If the blond had to pinpoint when the change occurred it was probably the day he'd found the Sage crying outside his Spire. The day the recluse remembers, with embarrassing clarity, that he had kissed the Sage. Had such possessive thoughts about the other cookie. The hermit was immensely grateful that the scholar was asleep when it happened. Otherwise he was sure he'd have never heard the end of it. Things had changed though. Making him wonder if the illustrious Sage of Truth had been awake and heard, and felt, everything.
 
Taking place a few weeks after the events of 'Negative Review'. Truthless Recluse has to handle the realisation that he's in love with the Sage of Truth, and the terrifying thought that the Sage might just love him back.
 
He doesn't handle it well.

summary:
Shadow Milk Cookie no podía dormir. Algo lo empujaba por los pasillos vacíos del castillo, hacia una luz que se filtraba por una puerta entreabierta.
Dentro, lo que encontró no era lo que esperaba.
Pure Vanilla Cookie y Truthless Recluse —dos mitades del mismo ser, dos versiones de un mismo hombre— estaban enredados en un encuentro íntimo que no estaba destinado a ser visto. Ropas desparramadas. Cuerpos descubiertos. Respiración entrecortada.
La orden de Truthless fue clara: "Lárgate."
Pero la invitación de Pure Vanilla fue más tentadora: "El más, mejor, ¿no crees?"
Shadow Milk, curioso, sinvergüenza y siempre hambriento de experiencias nuevas, cruzó el umbral. No para interrumpir. Para unirse.
Lo que siguió fue una danza de tres cuerpos que se buscaron en la penumbra, entre caricias que mordían y besos que consumían. Pure Vanilla, paciente y devorador. Truthless, brusco y hambriento. Shadow Milk, en el medio, siendo tocado por ambos, siendo llenado por ambos, siendo visto por ambos de maneras que no sabía que necesitaba.
Esta es la historia de una noche. De un encuentro. De tres cookies que, por unas horas, dejaron de ser reyes, bestias y títeres para ser solo carne y deseo.

summary:
They were not born monsters. They were Virtues - living ideals shaped by the Witches to guide Earthbread.
Eons after their corruption, the Beasts live in an uneasy peace-freed from the Silver Tree, bound by fragile truces with their Ancient counterparts, and tied together by history they refuse to name.They gather, they clash, they endure. They love. They destroy. They pretend the past is dead.
It isn't.
Within their Soul Jams, something stirs.
What once guided them has twisted into something cruel-conscious reflections of the very ideals they abandoned. They exist to remember, to mock, and to force the Beasts to face what they buried beneath deceit, destruction, apathy, sloth, and silence.
This is not a story about salvation.
It is a story about power, guilt, and identity-about what remains when virtues rot, and whether a monster can survive meeting the part of itself that still remembers what it was meant to be.
Because the Soul Jams were never silent. They were only waiting.

Truthless Recluse wrapped his hand around the other one immediately.
And as such, the sound ceased. The beast slid their hand down effortlessly, flicking off a lock of his hair—showing off, proud like a peacock.
"My my, all bark no bite," Shadow Milk snickered, though it wasn't the gentle, friendly kind of a noise. "You always promise gold and deliver bronze."
Truthless resisted the evident bait. He did not even touch the hook, really. Silence echoed where there was a cacophony, and his shoulders sloped inward, until only the shadows were gracing his face.
Beneath the washed gold of his bangs, grinned. The corners of his lips were pulled and oh did he chuckle. 
"What's so funny, eh?"
"Nothing," he replied dismissively, pulling Shadow Milk to wish to pry. "I think I get it now."
The hermit gave himself less time to recover. He already moved his hand back on the keys, much to the beast's shock. Strangely enough to have the other's lips part.
"Hey—" he uttered.
A ring of the piano followed.

Cookies were meant to be nothing but simple delights baked, shared, and forgotten. No one imagined they could ever become something more… until a witch made a fateful mistake. In her cluttered kitchen, potions spilled seeping into the dough and sugar. When the batch emerged from the oven, the impossible had happened: the Cookies were alive.
Word of such a discovery traveled through the covens. Witches everywhere began experimenting, each crafting their own living creations. What began as curiosity soon deepened into affection, then love. These cookies were no longer seen as treats, but children of flour and magic.
Yet the human world was cruel and unsafe for cookiekind. To protect them, the witches joined their power and wove an entirely new realm—a kingdom hidden from mortal eyes. Still, the Cookies were young, their hearts unshaped, their purpose unclear.
It was then that a wise witch proposed a daring solution. Together with her coven, she forged guardians—not rulers, but guides. Embodiments of ideals. Teachers of right and wrong. From this vision, the Virtues were born, destined to lead the Cookies and shape the destiny of their magical kingdom.

Silent Salt’s breath hitched just barely audible, but enough. His eyes flicked up, uncertain, as Dark Cacao’s shadow crossed over him. Then he leaned in, his forehead meeting Silent Salt’s, the touch firm and grounding. The cold of steel met the warmth of dough where the cracks ran deep.
And he drew in a breath, the sound of it catching in his throat, his hands hovering uselessly at his sides, fingers twitching like he wanted to reach back but couldn’t bring himself to.
He closed the distance himself.
It was timid, but his lips brushed against Dark Cacao’s, cold and cracked, tasting faintly of salt and ash.
The other Cookie, startled at first, took a sharp intake of breath, breaking between them; his hand froze where it was resting against Salt’s jaw, yet he didn’t pull away. His fingers curled instead, steadying himself against the other’s cheek, his thumb pressing into the fractured surface. For a moment, the chill of Silent Salt’s touch sank into him, meeting the heat that lived behind his armor, and it was honest.
When they finally parted, Dark Cacao’s breath trembled and he didn’t move away, only lowered his gaze, roughened and dragged over gravel.

Staying here instead of going where?

summary:
Some things are not meant to last.
Pure Vanilla knows that. He has always known that.
And yet—when offered something fragile, something uncertain, something that should never have worked in the first place… he finds himself reaching for it anyway.
It begins simply enough. A conversation. A choice. A quiet agreement between two unlikely sides.
From there, it becomes something more.
Something softer.Something steady.Something that begins to feel… real.
There is comfort in that. In routine. In familiarity. In the quiet assurance that, for once, things can remain unchanged.
And when something is repeated enough—given time, patience, and just the right amount of hope—it’s easy to believe in it.
Easy to settle into it.
Easy to forget that it was never meant to last at all.
…
Maybe then it doesn’t fall apart all at once.

summary:
I was born into a shadow that was never mine,Forced to carry fractures I did not create.
 
Every crack in me was gilded,A thin sheen of borrowed beauty-Like a carnival mask over the hollowness beneath.
 
Every hope I carried belonged to another,Handed down like a curse.
 
And if a shattered vase is pieced togetherAgain and again with gold,Does it ever remember what it truly was…Or is it only a lie dressed in stardust?
 
Every mended seam tremblesUnder the weight of its own impermanence.
 
Even as life and death alike crumble within it,The vase endures-
 
Not whole,Not itself,Only gilded,Only watched,Only haunted.
 
And perhaps, in its silence, it knows:To be broken againIs the only truth it will ever own.

summary:
Early in the Valley’s days, long before it would have a primary city that grew loud with trade bells and caravan horns, the land was scattered with villages – small clusters of stone and fire nestled between desert flats, red canyons, and jagged mountain spines. At the heart of it all stood Dragon’s Maw, the growing center of imports and exports, its name earned from the way the land curved inward like a great beast at rest. A day’s travel from the Maw lay a smaller village: Garra de Fuego. Strength in Garra de Fuego was not measured by power alone, but by endurance, restraint, and the will to keep the fire alive for others. It was here that Fenix was born, long before he would walk Fuego Road and ascend the Great Greenish-Red Dragon’s mountain, long before the decay of his own body.
(In Short: Long before Fire Spirit was Fire Spirit, God of the Eternal Flame, he was once a mortal human. Dragon's City has yet to solidify in the Valley, called Dragon's Maw at the time. summary:
Ever since Shadow Milk’s redemption, Pure Vanilla's life had flourished and bloomed in ways he would’ve never expected. He had a beautiful, lively kingdom and a wonderful community. Most of all, his other half, his soulmate, now lived in his walls.
But in a field of beautiful flowers, there’s always a stubborn weed.
A weed that’d been living with Pure Vanilla since his birth, and still haunted him even now. No matter how much it was plucked, by himself or others, it always came back, and it will always come back.
But how rough can you pull a weed, until it never comes back? Until delicate petals overshadow its growth? Until all you can do is be mesmerized by the good, so that the bad is barely recognizable?
How much can Shadow Milk keep pulling, and pulling, and pulling, until his beloved can do nothing else but focus on a gorgeous expanse of flowers? Until he can do nothing else but focus on him?
OR:
Pure Vanilla has had body dysphoria his entire life, and he’s reminded of his dislike for his body every single day. Shadow Milk’s duty is to make sure that the only thing he can focus on is just how beautiful he is, and how good he can make him feel, regardless of what he was born as.

summary: For a long time, everything in the Dark Cacao Kingdom was almost perfect.The halls were cold, the skies often gray, and the guards didn’t believe in smiling—but inside the castle, there was warmth. It lived in quiet mornings and louder arguments, mismatched teacups, and the occasional flower tucked behind a war general’s ear.Pure Vanilla, all sunbright laughter and insufferable habits—like braiding Cacao’s hair when he was grumpy—balanced out the king’s frost. He kissed his forehead in front of the guards just to watch him twitch. He called love a language spoken best through touch… so Dark Cacao learned to speak it.Their life was full of small, ridiculous joys. Cacao pretending not to like the cinnamon biscuits but always stealing three. Vanilla teasing him until he almost smiled.It wasn’t perfect. But it was theirs.Until one morning, the tide brought something in.A body. A face like Pure Vanilla’s—but wrong. A version that had never escaped the god Shadow Milk Cookie. A version twisted by years of cruelty, wearing trauma like perfume and smiling with something too hungry to be kind.Pure Vanilla saw someone worth saving.Dark Cacao saw a disaster waiting to happen.

There was a time when Mystic Flour Cookie believed that nothingness was better than pain.
There was a time when Dark Cacao Cookie believed that loneliness was the price of ruling.

When their paths crossed at the summit of the Snow-Covered Flour Mountain of Nirvana, he had his sword drawn and she had her eyes closed.
There was no battle.
There was a question no one had asked her in a thousand years:

She looks down at her hands, to see they are no longer those of a Witch, but a Cookie. Red, and burnt.
It takes little time to realize where she is.Undeniably, Dark Enchantress Cookie is dead. She recalls, now—what she felt a moment ago. Her body falling apart, the melted and ever-shifting dough reducing to dust as the sunset dawned upon her one last time. Her memories, flashing in front of her rapidly, from start to end.

summary:
Salt tilts his head curiously, stirring a little sugar into his tea before speaking. "Hey," he starts, voice casual but intrigued. "The other day I saw this weird thing where, uh, when you shake a jar of honey just right…it kind of sloshes like liquid for a second but then it instantly hardens again? Like magic."
He blinks at Fount expectantly, clearly hoping the Fount of Knowledge could explain such an odd observation. Fount’s expression dims instantly at the question—his pencil pausing mid-stroke. He hates when cookies treat him like an encyclopedia, constantly bombarding him with random inquiries just pbecause he’s “the Fount of Knowledge”. It makes him feel…reduced to his knowledge, not seen as a cookie. Even if he's made for that purpose and that purpose alone, he's also the only Virtue that doesn't have a life outside of his duties.
"It's just viscosity," he says simply, not elaborating further.
Or
Fount wants to be seen as him, not the Fount of Knowledge.

Shadow Milk looked down, his stuttered breath hitching as he gazed dazedly at the serrated blade that had impaled him.
His hands found their ways up to his wound, fingers shakily enclosing the blade. The sword was pulled back from his stomach with a wet splutter, before jam started flowing from the wound.

And for the first time in a while, he felt fear.

summary:
"Fine?" Truthless Recluse scoffed. "You boiled up shortly after you went out. If you are lucky enough, the fever might've already subsided."
"The… fever?"
Silence lingered, as if the hermit was giving the virtue time to process the information—somehow guessing that it was necessary. Fount's lip was pulled when he was in thought.
Fever. He should've expected as much, but it did not make it any easier to accept. What a foolish condition.
"…Right." Nodding, he closed his eyes in recall. That was right—what he knew is that he was with the witches, returned, and then the strangeness overtook him. But now that he awoke (as unusual as it was to sleep) he knew he was ready for the day.
"Thank you," Fount started. "For being here, I mean. I think that I can now return to the… usual, you know?"
The hermit sighed. He raised up a scroll to read from, face unimpressed and brow arched. "Dear Knowledge," he quoted. "I am aware the sugarshrooms that are labeled as poisonous are those with red hats and pink icings. However, the one I had found has icings similiar to white. Is it okay to eat said mushroom? How much of it is fine?"

And just when they'd start to think the story was about to get boring – when you'd think the (handsome) king in red robes was about to get his happy ending… with a flick of the quill, he's ten feet deep into the worst situation you could possibly imagine. And just like that, you're paying attention again – will he find a way out? Or was this really the end this time?
How stupid is that? Of course he was going to find a way out, he always did. Do you still truly believe that the hundredth time will be any different, just because it's an even three-digit number? He was practically immortal.
Shadow Milk wasn't a fool – he noticed eventually. He was the main character, therefore he was immortal. You can't kill off the main character without making the story come to an end – at least not in this case.
 
Or...
 
After realizing his own importance in the story, Shadow Milk rebels. The author doesn't have control over his character anymore, therefore gets mad and attempts to regain control over him by sending him a beautiful faerie prince, which she could use to lure him back into the tale.

summary:
When petals begin to bloom in Pure Vanilla Cookie’s lungs, they are pale at first, soft and almost beautiful, like a quiet confession he never meant to speak aloud. But beauty rots quickly in a world ruled by suspicion.
The Ancients do not see a dying friend. They see corruption. They see weakness. And when the truth spills from his mouth along with blood and flowers - that the source of his affliction is a Beast - they do not offer comfort. They offer judgment. Cast out not for sin, but for loving the wrong soul, Pure Vanilla is abandoned at the edge of a faith he once embodied.
In the shadows beyond their light, he finds the very being who caused his illness - and for the first time, the petals bloom without pain. In that fragile, forbidden reciprocity, a new Soul Jam is born… and it does not shine.  It Instantly fractures. It darkens. It chooses him as he chooses it. And when he rises again, it will not be as an Ancient. It will be as something far older than forgiveness - the Sixth Beast.

summary: After his defeat, the powerful yet broken Shadow Milk is stripped of his deceiving illusions and left vulnerable. He hides in a desolate corner of Earthbread, haunted by both his wicked past and fragmented memories of his time as the Fount of Knowledge.He is found not by a foe, but by a small, unassuming cookie who sees through his shattered facade with simple honesty. Shadow Milk initially tries his old tricks, but the cookie's genuine compassion forces him to confront his manipulative nature and loneliness.When his new companion is endangered, Shadow Milk faces a choice: rely on his destructive deceit or risk his fragile new self by embracing the truth. He chooses the latter, and his power transforms. Instead of cruel lies, it creates transient illusions that heal and inspire, reflecting a newfound balance between bitter truth and sweet fantasy.Shadow Milk never fully abandons his theatrical persona, but his theatrics now stem from genuine joy and hard-won wisdom. summary:
Ah… This cafe was not popular, was not unknown either. But it had a place in my life for sure. I just couldn't stop myself from coming here to take inspirations. It was at a place where you can watch many pass by. Seeing with who or what they talk, what they do, what they express and where they go. Their interactions was my inspirations for books. They seemed interesting so I wrote them. Maybe someday I'll write my own. But the thing I have wondered was, "Will I have a life like one of my stories?". Who knows?
...But today I found out that, the thing I wondered had come close. Something akin to a story in a book had happened to me...
A person, someone I haven't seen here do shifts before, had bought my order. Then asked me if I had anything else needed. To not seem uncaring I lifted my head from my laptop and answered. Or tried... What I saw before me, the person, was beautiful. Like they got out of a well written story. And the sun coming from the window just near my table was creating a more stunning look. Why haven't I seen them around here before?..
Or
Fate has plans for everyone. Good or bad, all of them will come true...

title: Shadow Milk’s Guide to Failing at Villainy
author: Kit_The_Sigma
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
relationships: Pure Vanilla Cookie/Shadow Milk Cookie (Cookie Run)
summary: Shadow Milk, the kingdom’s most dramatically menacing villain, has a simple plan: intimidate, threaten, and watch the Vanilla Kingdom crumble under his perfectly orchestrated villainy. He is excellent at darkness, sarcasm, and brooding. Unfortunately, Pure Vanilla Cookie is not only immune to intimidation, but somehow manages to smile, thank him, and accidentally ruin every plan. What follows is a chaotic dance of slow-burn chaos: Shadow Milk attempts sabotage, hand-to-hand intimidation, and brooding monologues, only to be met with clueless kindness, baffling politeness, and the occasional accidental hug. Pure Vanilla, confused beyond reason, is certain he’s doing nothing more than being polite—but Shadow Milk is increasingly convinced that the only thing more dangerous than himself is… feelings. From hand-holding incidents to public arguments mistaken for flirtation, from accidental team-ups to catastrophically failed threats, the book chronicles a rivalry spiraling into romance. It’s a story of sarcasm versus innocence, darkness versus chaos, and the hilariously unpredictable journey of two cookies learning that the “enemy” they’ve been fighting might just be the one who gets under their shadowy, sugar-coated heart.

summary:
Pure Vanilla thinks he’s a saint. He’s spent a lifetime being the perfect heir, the perfect friend, the perfect king. He thinks he’s observing Shadow Milk from a distance—the silent prop-maker in the circus wings, the boy who lied to put a roof on top of his head, the man who wears a smile like a weapon on stage.
He thinks he’s going to "unmask" him.What Pure Vanilla doesn't realize is that Shadow Milk has been observing him, too. Shadow Milk isn't a victim to be saved; he’s a jester who knows that every saint has a rot underneath. Shadow Milk doesn't want Pure Vanilla's pity; he wants his shadow.
 
Pure Vanilla is prepared to love Shadow Milk’s trauma. But Shadow Milk is the only one brave enough to love Pure Vanilla's selfishness, his arrogance, and the parts of him that aren't "Pure" at all.

“Wait— Golden Cheese Cookie… Please wait.”
Golden Cheese froze mid-step, and carefully she finally turned her head, just enough for White Lily to catch her profile; the gold of her skin catching the dim candlelight like burnished metal, and her eyes, when they met White Lily’s, were unflinching.

Golden Cheese’s face was a map she had studied once too many times, she wasn’t quite sure when it had begun or if she ever stopped, but even now, with the chasm of stretching wider, her eyes moved without her willing it to, tracing the graceful slope of Golden Cheese’s neck, the slight downturn of her mouth, and the lines at the edges of her eyes that deepened when she was tired or resolute.

There is nothing in her embrace. No love, no hate, no stress, no peace. His body is in ecstasy, her pillowy body rolling over him, washing away his worries from before any of this happened. His mind is elsewhere, somewhere deep, away.
She was hot. A strange, emanating warmth left her like the summer sun. It felt like he was melting. She was seemingly tireless, black eyes trained on his face, scrutinizing. He felt ashamed to enjoy this, a tinge of fear making his body tremble beneath her.

author: Fumusu
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
relationships: Eternal Sugar Cookie & Shadow Milk Cookie (Cookie Run)
summary:
The Garden of Delights has no thorns.
Eternal Sugar Cookie built it that way: a place where no cookie would ever suffer again, where happiness is eternal and pain does not exist. Only peace. Only sweetness. Only her, watching over every soul that chooses to stay.
Then Shadow Milk Cookie arrives.
He does not come to stay. He comes to mock, to provoke, to remind her that even paradises have cracks. He comes disguised as a lady, with a smile made entirely of sharp edges and a question he never asks out loud:
—And you? Who takes care of you when everyone falls asleep?
She should cast him out. She should hate him. She should stop waiting for his next visit.
But serpents always find a way back into the garden.
And she always leaves the door slightly open.

Sonic had escaped from G.U.N.'s experimentation, with the help of Aeigus. Thousands of G.U.N. Agents hot on his trail while breaking through to the surface with renewed vigor. He couldn't understand! He'd proven himself to be the most trustworthy hero he could be. Kind to all civilians regardless of how they treat him.
Yet, this is how they repayed him. Anytime someone was reminded of his existence, glares came from all directions. Not just the Mobians, but the Humans too. Bothered by him surviving on the last source of energy and food he had. Like he didn't deserve any of it.
And as time passed by, Sonic gave in to routine. Days came and went. Turning into weeks, then months. By then, everyone was too disturbed by the incident to even talk to him. New subjects came in, none of them came out. Screams echoing from all corners of the room. He wanted to save them, but it was too late for most of them. And the ones that survived, the ones that he tried to help, beat him till he stopped. Not wanting to accept help from the one who they thought helped put them here.
If this was what they wanted, then fine. Hero or not, whatever happens to this world wasn't his problem anymore. Freedom was.

summary: They say the snow never stops falling in the Cacao Kingdom, and for nearly a year, it mourned without end. Its king—disciplined, unwavering, the very spine of its law—was gone, no trace left behind but the echo of his last command. His name, unetched in the altar of the fallen, remained untouched not from negligence, but from stubborn belief. He could not fall. He would not.They were wrongSomewhere far from the mountains, where no sun dares to settle and laughter curls like smoke through the cracks of a tower, something began to unravel.A jester waits there.Now the color of his soul jam begins to shift, blue-laced, traced with a pale white quiet but steady—its warmth bleeding into something colder, stranger. He tells himself it’s only exhaustion, that duty still anchors him. That he is still the man they remember.Plans are drawn beneath starlight. Kingdoms are next. And when Shadow Milk can no longer stand, it is Cacao who carries him—without question.The hero is not lost. He simply… chose a different ending.And the world, whether it weeps or bows, will have no choice but to follow.Updates randomly weekly

Because other cookies don’t know their rightful place as you do, Venom Dough Cookie. Good, you’re kept in line, and we shall do it for all of cookiekind."
The prototypes of the Ultimate Cookie had only known rejection, faked kindness, and pain. So much pain that they wanted to be free of, but have no choice to serve until the bitter end. They were twisted, manipulated, and hurt time and time again. Treated as objects, treated as only tolerable disappointments the moment they were brought into the world. And sadly, they were never given another choice to prove themselves; they were told to keep going, fulfill their master's ideals that they were forced into.

summary:
His breath came out in short, shallowed gasps. The snow, the biting chill of the wind, it was all the same. Too familiar, too much like home. Yet, he knew all too well that this wasn't the kingdom he knew. However, did he know the very place he was raised in as much as his title suggests? Dark Choco's lone eye blinked a few times, as if that was going to fix it. He wiped his hands on his shirt, his blood smearing onto the fabric. His mind still couldn't comprehend all that had happened. It all happened way too fast. Nothing ever felt real. Well, not anymore. All they could ever do was walk forward, bracing themselves for whatever lay ahead.

Burning Spice is the God-Emperor of his realm. Absolute. Powerful. And he is so fucking bored. This realm has nothing to offer him. Every day the same thing happens over and over again. No one to challenge him, no change in his ever monotonous life. Even the destruction he unleashed on different neighboring kingdoms and realms did little to satiate his boredom or alter his life in any meaningful way. It was fun, for sure. But after the euphoria of battle and carnage wore off, he was bored again.
Until tales of a distant kingdom filled with great mountains and white peaks, with its ruler, an immortal Empress, reached his ears. Tales of her beauty, of her granting mortals who made the pilgrimage to her any wishes they desired--as long as she deemed the wish worthy. Then, there were tales of her mystical powers that had allowed her to maintain her rule for centuries...
He'll see for himself if these words have any merit in truth. If she can relieve him of his boredom, even if for only a little while.

Perhaps it was a notebook he was gifted back then? Had White Lily accidentally left it on his side? Pure Vanilla was puzzled. White Lily would not want it back, not when it would bring her nothing but bad memories. It was such a pretty book, too. He mindlessly looked through the pages. Maybe he could make it a new journal, if only to record his travels. After all, this place was only the beginning of his journey throughout Earthbread.
 
Having made up his mind, Pure Vanilla pulled out a quill and wrote on the first page.
 
January 11, 20XX. Blueberry Yoghurt Academy. It’s been a long time.
 
Immediately, the dark ink sank into the page and vanished.
 
Pure Vanilla blinked, and the page was blank. Then, slowly, a new sentence appeared, like another person was writing back. The words were smooth and elegant.
 
Hello? Has it really been that long? May I ask who you are?

…you will crumble, idiot.
The thought is a vow whispered to the slumbering saint—and to himself.
And I will be—
Shadow Milk Cookie’s form casts an awfully long shadow across the bed. 
His clawed fingers stretch—black streaks poised to carve into dough, by the cruelty of silhouette alone. 
He does not bring them down. Does not rake the declaration of war into skin that is too soft, too warm. 
Cyan, sea, and the dozens of writhing eyes narrowed within the black of his hair remain fixed upon the pinched brow of a saint—a saint forced into a most cumbersome rest, on the eve of battle.
You will CRUMBLE, and… I will… be...

But as you run –  hot, wet breath in your neck –  it hits you.
 
That sweet scent.After escaping the beasts in the forest, you drag your beaten and battered body back into the Garden of Delights. And despite your best efforts, you can't hide your injuries from the kind, watchful eye of your wife.

There once was the Wind and the Fire.
The Wind, calm, responsible, always fulfilled his duty of protecting the forest and healing fallen spirits.
The Fire, energetic, impulsive, wasn't fond of doing what he got ordered to, claiming there are so many things more interesting than being a Guardian.
These two, although differed from each other in lots of ways, usually were on rather friendly terms. There was just one thing to it...
They both saw their relationship differently.
Wind Archer, most of times annoyed by the Fire's attitude, did not quite like the guy.
Fire Spirit, often irritated by the Wind's coldness and firmness, saw him as killjoy yet nice when he wasn't scolding him.
One day, they both end up in other universes, ones that aren't theirs, and encounter different versions of each other.
Wind Archer and Fire Spirit need to find a way back home as quick as possible, for the escape will disappear in no time.
Will they manage to reunite and change something in their lives, or will they get trapped in alternate timelines forever and won't see each other again?

summary:
The Jester arrives—bells chiming too bright against stone and incense, laughter spilling where there should be reverence. She smiles too easily, stands too close, lingers as if she has nowhere else to go. A court jester with a permanent smile and magic that bends space, and she is very determined to stay.
Dark Cacao’s kingdom is built on sacrifice, her halls lined with the names of warriors who died for her rule. She endures them because she must, not because she wishes to.
At night, Cacao finds herself thinking of those who no longer have to stand watch. Of rest. Of stillness. Of how tempting it might be to disappear. How some nights the queen envies how final their rest is.
Shadow Milk fills the quiet on purpose. She becomes noise, color, interruption. Where others approach the queen with expectation, Shadow Milk brings disorder instead.
If something begins to grow in the space between lanternlight and shadow—something warmer, something dangerous—It is simply what happens when two restless souls choose, for now, not to be alone. And yet… neither of them will name it.

Clotted Cream—renowned superhero agent, polished and impossibly confident—had shown up in Pure Vanilla’s life like a storm wrapped in a tailored suit. When the man first asked him to work for the Silver Tree Super Hero Agency, Pure Vanilla had honestly thought it was a joke. Or a scam. Or some elaborate misunderstanding.
Yes, his healing quirk was strong. Exceptionally so, according to the records. But his vision problems made fieldwork impossible. He couldn’t fight villains, couldn’t patrol cities or leap into danger like the heroes on the news. And he had accepted that long ago.
Against his better judgment, he had said yes.
There were many reasons for that decision, but the most honest one was money.
Between his part-time coffee shop job, White Lily’s reporting work for a fairly large news channel that paid little unless you broke a major story, and Shadow Milk’s teacher salary, they were barely staying afloat. Rent came due faster every month, groceries cost more, and villain attacks were growing more frequent and more destructive. Insurance barely covered anything anymore.

Fire Spirit has never done things halfway. When he loves, he loves fiercely, wholly. His trust, although seldom bequeathed in its true self, is given fully. The two clash constantly in this way—but somehow, they ended up here, with each other.
The night is dark and empty, the silence is too loud.
Fire Spirit can't let go.
